title: Model serving SLO shock-testing runbook — 30-day lab
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical runbook for a 30-day shock-testing lab targeting model-serving SLOs. Goal: validate the SLO signal pipeline, fallback routing, and error-budget responses under controlled stress and partial-failure scenarios.

Scope (what we will exercise):
- Single-model endpoint (gpt-small-quant) and a multi-model route that can fallback to gpt-medium-approx.
- Traffic patterns: steady baseline + sudden 3x-10x spike, slow memory leak, and node preemption events.
- Observability: latency p95/p99, token throughput, error rate (5xx and decoded model-failures), queue length, KV cache hit-rate, model-switch events in routing logs.
- Control-plane reactions: autoscaler triggers, routing fallbacks, canary rollback, and alerting.

Primary goals / hypothesis:
1) Hypothesis: Automatic fallback to medium-approx keeps p95 < 750ms for 90% of spike runs without exhausting error budget.
2) Hypothesis: KV cache hit-rate drop explains >20% of token-latency regressions during sustained spikes.
3) Hypothesis: Autoscaler cooldown tuning currently causes 2-4 minute underprovisioning window.

Success criteria (pass/fail):
- No customer-visible latency SLO violation in more than 5% of spike runs (SLO = p95 < 500ms for hosted-tier; for lab we accept 750ms threshold).
- Error budget consumption per 24h window < 5% during the test (as measured by SLO telemetry pipeline).
- Fallback events logged with correlation IDs and roll-forward ability (can be turned off for final test).

Metric definitions and dashboards to use:
- latency.p95, latency.p99 (for token generation endpoint)
- errors.rate (5xx, model-runtime-timeouts, decode_errors)
- tokens/sec and requests/sec per model route
- kvcache.hit_rate per instance
- routing.fallback.count and routing.fallback.latency
- autoscaler.scale_events and provisioning_time
Dashboards: infra/serving/latency-summary, infra/serving/kvcache, product/slo-telemetry/model-serving.

Experiment matrix (30-day cadence):
- Week 0 (prep, canary): smoke test baseline, verify dashboards, link telemetry, run one controlled 3x spike for 15 minutes.
- Week 1 (spike study): five 1-hour runs with 3x and 5x traffic bursts; record fallback behavior.
- Week 2 (degradation modes): memory leak simulation on 10% of nodes; two 4-hour runs to observe autoscaler and node recovery.
- Week 3 (preemption window): simulate preemptive node kill during high KV-cache usage; test node drain and request retry logic.
- Week 4 (combined full-run): combined 5x spike + 10% node preemptions + synthetic downstream storage latency; run one 6-hour scenario.
Notes: runs should be scheduled during low real-customer impact windows in staging. Document all environment variables and config snapshots before each run.

Pre-run checklist (must be green before any test):
- [ ] baseline capture: export last 7 days of SLO telemetry to artifacts bucket (s3://redwood-lab/msrt/shock-tests).
- [ ] alert mute: create ephemeral alert suppression tickets for non-customer channels with TTL matching the run.
- [ ] canary endpoint: spin up isolated canary route configured with same runtime but separate capacity reservation.
- [ ] observability hooks: tracing enabled, request IDs forwarded, KV-cache metrics at instance granularity.
- [ ] runbook printed & owners assigned in Slack channel #msrt-shock-tests.

Run-time playbook (for the operator running the experiment):
1) Kickoff: announce in #msrt-shock-tests with run id (use timestamp).
2) Start traffic generator (locust/vegeta) against canary route using pre-made scenario files (repo: infra/test-harness/scenarios/model-spike).
3) Monitor dashboards, have SRE and runtime engineer on-call watching p95, errors, fallback counts.
4) At first signs of SLO breach (p95 > lab-threshold for two consecutive 1-min windows):
   - pause traffic generator, collect flamegraphs and heap profiles, snapshot routing table, collect KV-cache hotkeys.
   - If fallback occurred: capture routing logs and associated correlation IDs.
   - If autoscaler did not provision in expected window: escalate to infra-oncall and mark note for cooldown tuning.
5) After each run: store artifacts, tag run in linked JIRA ticket, and update experiment spreadsheet.

Post-run analysis template (what to capture):
- run id, duration, traffic multiplier, config snapshot (runtime flags), snapshot of model weights/commit hash, p95/p99 summary, error breakdown, fallback count and duration, autoscaler events, KV cache hit-rate trend.
- short written verdict: PASS/FAIL and top 3 root-cause leads.
- next steps captured as discrete tickets (owner + due date).

Roles & contacts (primary):
- Experiment owner: Ravi Patel (run coordination, artifact collection) — @ravi
- Runtime engineer: Dmitri Volkov (kernel selection, perf knobs) — @dmitri
- SRE lead: Ava Martinez (oncall escalation, alert tuning) — @ava
- Observability: Sofia Chen (dashboards, telemetry pipeline) — @sofia
- Program stakeholder: Lina O’Connell (product SLO owner) — @lina
Emergency escalation: paging pager duty SRE_Primary -> SRE_Manager.

Runbook snippets / useful commands (staging cluster):
- start traffic: infra/test-harness/bin/attack --scenario spike-3x --route canary-gpt-small --duration 3600 --outdir /tmp/run-<id>
- snapshot config: kubectl -n serving get configmaps runtime-config -o yaml > /tmp/run-<id>/runtime-config.yaml
- collect heap: curl http://<instance>:9200/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/run-<id>/heap-$(hostname).pprof
- trace examples: curl -H "x-trace-id: run-<id>" http://canary.example/api/generate?prompt=probe

Artifacts and storage convention:
- All artifacts go to s3://redwood-lab/msrt/shock-tests/<run-id>/ with subfolders: logs/, traces/, profiles/, dashboards/, reports/
- Filenames: <run-id>__<artifact-type>__<timestamp>.json (or .pprof/.svg)

Communication playbook (internal & customer-facing):
- Internal: real-time updates to #msrt-shock-tests; post-run summary in #eng-all with link to report if run caused any customer impact.
- Customers: do not contact unless run creates a visible impact; if so, CS to coordinate and product to draft a short note.

Risk mitigations and safety rails:
- Use canary-only capacity unless we explicitly toggle to broader pool.
- Auto-abort if errors.rate spikes above 20% for more than 5 minutes.
- Limit test to 3 simultaneous experiments in the cluster.

Open questions / things to iterate on (notes-to-self):
- Do we add synthetic model degradation (soft-fail outputs) to test quality-based SLOs? (Lina wants an example).
- How to compute the customer-visible SLO delta for approximate-fallback models (we need a calibrated human-eval set).
- Can we expose a lightweight simulation mode for autoscaler to run faster in staging? Ticket created: MSRT-4177.

Appendix A — quick checklist for postmortem ticket template:
- Title: <run-id> shock test <short-failure-summary>
- One-line summary, timeline, artifacts attached, three root-cause hypotheses, mitigation and config changes, follow-up tickets with owners and due dates.

Appendix B — quick links:
- Dashboard: https://app.observability.redwood/internal/dashboards/serving/latency-summary
- Run harness repo: https://github.com/redwood/infra-test-harness
- Telemetry pipeline docs: confluence:/display/MS/SLO+Telemetry

Ravi — quick todo before next review: add synthetic quality probe configs and align on acceptable fallback-quality delta with Lina.

-- end of runbook (informal notes / working draft)
